text:
emily: Hi team, I'm updating beneficiaries after a separation. Quick Q: do I need my ex-spouse's consent to change beneficiaries on the 401k? Also, will changing beneficiary affect vesting or employer match already deposited?

jean (People Ops): Short answers: 1) Usually you do NOT need spouse consent to name a non-spouse beneficiary unless your plan has a spousal consent requirement for married participants, 2) changing beneficiaries does not alter your vested balance or employer contributions already posted. Are you currently married on file?

emily: We're separated but not legally divorced; payroll still shows spouse on file. The portal won't let me pick a new primary beneficiary; it greys out the field and says "spousal consent required".

legal-bot: Legal: Many plans default-spouse-protection if marital status is "married" in HRIS. Spousal consent forms (notarized in some cases) are common when naming a non-spouse primary. Check your plan's SPD for exact requirements.

jean (People Ops): If the portal requires spousal consent we can 1) provide the plan's spousal consent form, 2) coordinate with payroll/legal if notarization is needed, or 3) in limited cases we can accept a domestic partner affidavit if eligible. Which would you prefer?

emily: I'd prefer to avoid getting notarized right now. Is there a way to designate a contingent beneficiary (like my mom) without changing primary? That would at least ensure something is set.

benefits-portal-bot: Benefits Portal: Portal enforces spousal-consent validation when participant marital_status == "married" in HRIS. You can add a contingent beneficiary but primary remains spouse until consent form uploaded and accepted by vendor. Contingent will be applied if primary predeceases participant.

jean (People Ops): You can absolutely add a contingent beneficiary without spouse consent. That is a good short-term step. If you want to change primary now we'd need spouse consent form signed and HRIS marital status update if marital status actually changed. We can also route a secure PDF to your spouse for e-sign if that helps.

emily: If spouse doesn't sign, can I still update beneficiary after divorce final? And how will that affect taxes or the ability to roll to an IRA?

legal-bot: Upon divorce final decree, spouse's beneficiary designation may be invalidated depending on state law and plan terms. After divorce you can update primary without consent. Beneficiary changes do not change taxation or rollover options on vested balances; only distributions trigger tax events. If there's a QDRO required for splitting plan assets, that is a separate legal process handled in divorce proceedings and must be submitted to plan administrator.

jean (People Ops): Practical next steps: 1) If you want immediate protection add contingent beneficiary via portal, 2) if you want primary changed now request the spousal consent form from us and we'll send an e-sign flow, 3) if divorce goes through later we can re-run beneficiary update without consent. Also, beneficiary changes do not change existing vesting or match amounts.

emily: Thanks! Please send the contingent add and the spousal consent e-sign link; I'll ask if they'd complete it but will plan for the contingent to be primary fallback. Appreciate it. :pray:

payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: Beneficiary changes must be accepted by the plan vendor prior to distribution events. No payroll impact for beneficiary updates.

jean (People Ops): On it @emily. I'll DM you the e-sign link and upload instructions. If you need an anonymous copy of plan SPD language about spousal consent for your records, I can attach that too.
